title: A Dixieland combo on Sundays at the Elks and Small's
summary: After the show, Scott leads a five-piece Dixieland group on Sundays.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, anyway, Alley Ross did the show. Well, the show ended. I come back uptown, naturally, and go down, gigging, and I played -- I didn't lose any time because I

worked the very next night and the very next night, kept on working. And one fellow wanted me to come down to the Elks with him. Something happened around there, I don't know. Said, oh, come on, -- you know how you go with fellows, just meet them, come on and have a couple of drinks.

We went down there, and the guy wanted me to put a band in there. I told him I -- he said, oh, this is just for Sundays, a couple of hours. We need some music and all like that. So they finally convinced me. No music, didn't need any. The fellows I chose knew everything. They knew everything. And I had five men in there, and we just played regular dixieland stuff, like that.

Ed Small called me, too, and told me every Sunday he wanted me to come in there with Dixie. Now, that meant that I worked twice on Sundays, afternoon and night. Well, when you keep that up, gradually -- of course, I was at home, getting my meals there, but gradually it'll tell on you later on. You can't feel it, you don't realize it, because you're happy, carefree.
